triage.author: Benjamin Scott
triage.text: Drove hours out of my way to the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library in Medora—because let’s be real, there’s not much else pulling people through that stretch of North Dakota. Got turned away at the door for not having a timed ticket. Explained the long drive, asked if there was any way to work with us, and the staff member looked almost insulted that I’d even asked. I’ve visited presidential libraries and the Smithsonian on the Fourth of July without this nonsense. You’re not the Louvre out there, folks. A little North Dakota hospitality would’ve gone a long way.

triage.author: Jerry Krug
triage.text:
I have visited other Presidential libraries (Lincoln, FDR, Truman, Eisenhower, Hoover, Ford, Carter) before this. I rate this a mediocre experience. Unsure it was worth the trip from Wisconsin.

I expected an introductory film. I expected more meat about accomplishments and consequences. Too much sizzle and not enough steak. The use of technology pandered, didn't enhance, except for the room where TR responded to questions from attendees. Attendees who didn't already know a lot about TR would not learn enough to understand why his presidency was so transformative. Glad we listened to an audiobook from the Edmund Morris trilogy during the drive to learn about TR.

The gift shop offerings are inadequate. Thought there were would be mounds of teddy bears with spectacles, a refrigerator magnet showing the building or a head/shoulders shot, and lots of books. After all, this is a library. TR himself published 56 books, but none were for sale. So much has been published about TR and those times, but only a few seemingly-random selections were available. I didn't think it would be possible to not buy something from the gift shop of a Presidential library, but we didn't.

triage.author: Steve Harter
triage.text: Would have been 5 stars but there were 200+ school children across 5 buses at the same time - we started at 10:00 AM. Too crowded and many exhibits were not usable due to congestion.

triage.author: Den Mac
triage.text:
I have to keep reminding myself this place only opened in July. The concept is good and the place is beautiful. However, there are flow issues inside. There needs to be better signage to match the map for timeline accuracy visiting of the different areas.
While there are a lot of beautiful artifacts, the description placards contain too small of print & some of the placards have words worn off already.
In the gift shop, I think maybe they didn't plan to be so busy because they were sold out of some basic items such as TR Library stickers.

In the cafe, they could be more efficient if they would have a menu visible from the line instead of not until you get to the counter. Very beautiful grounds and conveniently located near the Medora Musical.

triage.author: cdb
triage.text:
We visited on a Sunday at the end of October.  The Library is a beautiful facility in a serene setting.  The exterior blends in splendidly with the natural landscape.

We arrived early and sat inside in comfy chairs by huge picture windows.  I bought postcards first thing while there was no one in the gift shop.  Items are spendy, the postcards were $2.99 each.  There was no price by the display and thanks to the clerk, she made sure I knew how much I was going to be charged.  When it was our appointed time to enter the exhibits, there was a throng of people getting their pictures taken at the AI photo stations. We bypassed that option and started our visit.

My overall impression was favorable, although there were several letdowns for me.
CROWD SIZE:  Having just opened in July, this attraction is drawing sizable crowds and every display had people standing side by side to view display items and it was not easy to walk between the exhibit cases.  I could tell a lot of thought went into all the exhibits, but I was only able to see a few items without reading the information.  My advice is to check the website and see when there are a lot of unreserved times - I think that would allow for more 'elbow room' and the ability to take in the displays.
We experienced several of the themed rooms and they were all in working order and still had a new feeling.  I enjoyed the room where Teddy answered questions.
THE RESTROOM:  This was a serious disappointment and worth revision consideration by the organization.  I cannot speak to the restroom configuration by the cafe, but the one in the exhibit area had to have been someone's minimalist brainchild.  The stalls were arranged in a small area and were unisex. I think there were four regular stalls and one ADA.  When I got into a stall, either the man before me or another user had peed on the seat.  My husband said the one he used was in the same shape.  The common sink area could accommodate two people comfortably while stall users moved out into the sink space.  I get the concept, but separate restrooms are the way to go.  I cannot remember if there would have been room to plumb a urinal in each of the stalls.
FINDING THE EXIT:  OMG, when we'd pegged out our fun meter and wanted to leave, we had a dickens of a time finding the exit.  I can honestly say when we finally saw the signage, it was small and up high.  I would be interested to know what the emergency exit strategy is when it might be necessary to move several hundred people out of a crowded area.  The map we received at the start of our visit was of no help.  We looked for a docent to get help, but could not locate one.
GOOD TO KNOW:  I use walking poles for balance and had no problem with the ability to use them in this facility.  There was a water fountain with a water bottle filling station, so I assumed I could have brought my own water bottle.  People were wearing sling pouches/purses, so that would have been an option since the website specifically forbids backpacks.  Non-flash photography is fine.
DEFINITELY WORTH A SECOND VISIT:  I imagine as time goes by, visitation will relax and it will be easier to see what's on display inside the Library.  We'll give it a try again during the off season.  Personally we would avoid visiting in spring and summer.  We'll visit again in fall.

triage.author: Candyfsu
triage.text:
We explored the Theodore Roosevelt National Park and his presidential library, which just opened July 4 of this year. They are both open year round. We have never been to a presidential library before so we really didn’t know what to expect. We were very pleasantly surprised and had a fun afternoon! It was very interactive!

When you check in you are given a wristband with a compass to use throughout your visit.
TIP 1: If you have bought more than 1 ticket be sure to have others in your party enter THEIR OWN NAME and their email when you all check in at the kiosks. We didn’t know this at check-in, but as you do the interactive activities, the name on your ticket is what shows up. For example, we were able to have AI generated images (see pictures) but mine show my husband’s name instead of my own. Lesson learned.. which we had known that when we were checking in. I’m sure they’re still on a learning curve since the park just opened in July, but, this makes it more meaningful. Kind of a letdown to see my own images - with my husband’s name! When you finish the last activity , all of your interactions and images are emailed to you.

TIP 2: if you have an afternoon ticket reserved, go see the library part (building on right) FIRST. Our tickets were at 1 pm. We got done at 3:45. The library announced closing time at 4pm. When we realized we hadn’t even been inside the library part we went to go do a quick view since we supposedly had 15 more minutes. Nope. the library closed before 4 PM. Needless to say we were disappointed. Again, we had no idea how long the interactive side would take. Definitely would’ve gone to the library first.

If you plan to go to the library, you need to buy tickets in advance because they have timed entry so it doesn’t get overcrowded. It cost $26 per ticket. Well worth the price as we spent almost 3 hours just on the interactive portion, We didn’t even get to see the actual library! Oops.

The best parts for us? We made sure to check our progress (see all the small kiosks throughout) to check and see what we’ve done and what’s left to do! Glad we did that because we had missed some areas. We had our AI images done for all areas. Lots of fun to see ourselves in the old days! Hubby loved the interactive activity with cattle. You moved around to move the cattle back to their corral. I loved the Amazon 360° experience! Sit -or stand/ in the back to get the best view! Great day!

7.headline: Ratings holding at 4.81 across 47 reviews
paragraphs: 47 reviews in the last 7 days, up 16 on the previous 7 days. The average is up 0.1. 6.4% rated three stars or below.

Visitors are consistently praising the interactive exhibits, the building and the setting. The AI experience continues to divide a small minority: 95 reviews to date name it as the reason for a low rating, against heavy praise for the same feature. Low volume, but it is the most likely subject of a critical feature story.

The complaints that cost us stars cluster tightly. The most frequent is crowding inside the galleries (1 mention), followed by how visitors move through the galleries. These are operational and messaging fixes rather than problems with the experience itself, which is the better problem to have. Separately, 12 reviews are waiting on a reply and 4 are past our own service level.
